title: Membership in the index-tagged list locates a tail
statement: Let $t$ be a list over a type $\alpha$, and tag each entry of $t$ with its zero-based position, forming the list of pairs $(t_i, i)$. If a pair $(l, i)$ occurs among these tagged entries — equivalently, the entry of $t$ at position $i$ is $l$ — then deleting the first $i$ entries of $t$ leaves a nonempty list whose first element is $l$; that is, there is a list $\mathit{rest}$ with $t$ from position $i$ onward equal to $l$ prepended to $\mathit{rest}$.
hypotheses_covered: the pair $(l, idx)$ belongs to the index-tagged list of $t$
replaced:
If $(l, \mathit{idx}) \in t.\mathrm{zipIdx}$, then dropping $\mathit{idx}$ elements from $t$
yields a list starting with $l$, i.e.\ $t.\mathrm{drop}\,\mathit{idx} = l :: \mathit{rest}$
for some remaining tail.
